html:
Tokyo is the capital of Japan and the heart of the largest urban area in the world. Until 1868 it was called Edo.

Edo began as a small castle town on a bay of the Kanto plain; a local lord built the first Edo Castle in 1457. In 1590 Toyotomi Hideyoshi gave the region to Tokugawa Ieyasu, who made Edo his base. Once he became shogun in 1603, it was the real seat of power in Japan, while the emperor stayed in Kyoto. Lords had to spend every other year there with large retinues, and the city passed a million people in the early 1700s. It was a city of merchants, kabuki, woodblock prints and poets such as Basho.

After the Meiji Restoration the emperor moved in, and the city was renamed Tokyo, "eastern capital". It led Japan's rush to modernise:

  • Japan's first railway ran from Tokyo to Yokohama in 1872.
  • The Tokyo Stock Exchange opened in 1878.
  • The Great Kanto earthquake and fires of 1923 destroyed much of the city.
  • The Ginza Line of 1927 was Asia's first underground railway.

American fire raids in March 1945 burned much of the city and killed some 100,000 people in one night. Tokyo rebuilt fast: Sony was founded there in 1946, and it hosted the Olympics in 1964, the year the first bullet train linked it to Osaka.
sum: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and the heart of the largest urban area in the world. Until 1868 it was called Edo.
